text: The pipeline begins with input face images captured under varying illumination, guided by key stages outlined in the legend.
A three-dimensional morphable model is first fitted to the input to construct a baseline geometric proxy.
From this proxy, a surface normal map and semantic segmentation are extracted to distinguish regions such as bare skin and hair.
Next, shadow processing handles shaded areas across the face to isolate reliable photometric information.
Using light calibration and photometric stereo, the system combines the shadow analysis and proxy guidance into a refined geometric model.
Finally, a denoising step produces the detailed final three-dimensional face mesh along with the recovered surface albedo.
